openclaw.label: OpenClaw's own scheduler
openclaw.verify: openclaw cron list  — {JOB_NAME} must be listed, and its delivery must resolve to a real route. A delivery shown as `announce -> last` with `no route, will fail-closed` means the job will run every day and deliver nowhere: re-create it with an explicit `--channel <id>` (and `--to` where the channel needs one) so the operator actually receives the report.
openclaw.remove: openclaw cron list  (find the id for {JOB_NAME}, then: openclaw cron remove <jobId>)
openclaw.least_privilege: The --tools exec above is not optional padding: without it OpenClaw stores an unrestricted tool policy, and the job would wake each day able to write files, edit code, create further scheduled jobs and spawn sessions — while reading mail written by strangers. Keep the list to what one shell command needs. If your build rejects --tools, create the job without it and then restrict it with `openclaw cron edit`; do not leave it unrestricted. (Newer builds name this command group `openclaw automations`; `cron` is the alias that works on both.)

hermes.label: Hermes' own scheduler
hermes.least_privilege: Restrict what the job may do before you leave it unattended: it reads mail written by strangers, so it needs no terminal, browser or delegation toolsets. Set them per job with enabled_toolsets on the cronjob tool (for example enabled_toolsets=["file"]), or configure the `cron` platform once in `hermes tools`. Do not use --no-agent: that runs a script with no model, so nobody reads the mail. If the Atomic Mail skill is installed, add --skill atomicmail so the job does not depend on the command resolving on PATH.

claude-code.label: Claude Code's own scheduler
instruction: Use a **local** routine. While the credentials live on this machine, only a local routine can read them: a cloud routine runs on Anthropic infrastructure with no access to local files, so it cannot reach the credentials directory below. So the choice is made for you — local.

Create it with Routines -> New routine -> Local, schedule preset {PRESET}, or just ask in-session: create a local routine named {JOB_NAME} that runs {HUMAN} at {TIME} and does the following. Point it at a folder you trust, then press Run now once and approve the tools it asks for, so later runs do not stall on a permission prompt with nobody watching. A local routine only fires while the Desktop app is open and the computer is awake.
Do not use /loop for this. It is scoped to the current session and expires after seven days, so the inbox would quietly stop being checked.

Footnote — only if this inbox must be checked with the laptop closed: a **cloud** routine (Routines -> New routine -> Cloud, or /schedule in the CLI) fires even when this machine is off, but it cannot read local credentials, so it works only with Atomic Mail connected as a remote MCP connector (not the local stdio server). Minimum interval is one hour.
claude-code.verify: Ask: what scheduled tasks do I have? — {JOB_NAME} must be listed and Active.
claude-code.remove: Delete the {JOB_NAME} routine from the Routines list, or ask: delete the {JOB_NAME} scheduled task.
claude-code.least_privilege: A cloud routine runs fully autonomously — no permission prompts — and includes every connector on your account by default, each usable for writes without asking. Remove every connector the job does not need, leaving Atomic Mail. A local routine keeps its permission mode, so approve only the tools the one command needs on the first Run now.

block.least_privilege: Give the job the least it needs. It runs one command and reports back, and what it reads is mail written by strangers — so it needs no file writing, no editing, no creating further scheduled jobs, no spawning sessions. If this host supports a per-job tool allowlist, set it explicitly rather than accepting the default, which is usually every tool the host has. The read-only wording in the prompt is a line of text; the allowlist is the part that holds.
